content.text: For each of the runs, were any errors seen in at the console or in the logs?

It looks like the 144K run failed due to the "unable to delete staging" error noted in #sprint-migrate on Jan. 27.  See stack trace below.  Perhaps this is due to attempting to delete the staging directory while resources within this directory are still in process of being copied?
: now that a fix for the related ticket has been committed to 'master' (
would you be able to test if the issue in this ticket has also been resolved?

yes, the issue seems to be fixed after we tested with the latest migration utility. We also added more inodes on our filesystem during the last round of testing. So far we have tested 8 million objects migration without issue in both akurba and legacy type.

During high volume testing migration-utils did not complete specified limit switch object setting values. During one test of Akruba sourcetype, flat layout test where the limit was set to 4,000,000 the resume.txt file indicate only 554,695 object completed, and another test of 4 million Akruba sourcetype and pairtree layout 144,168 were completed.

comments.body: For each of the runs, were any errors seen in at the console or in the logs?

It looks like the 144K run failed due to the "unable to delete staging" error noted in #sprint-migrate on Jan. 27.  See stack trace below.  Perhaps this is due to attempting to delete the staging directory while resources within this directory are still in process of being copied?

 

DEBUG 14:35:07.056 (OCFLFedora4Client) createOrUpdateNonRDFResource: nlm:icid-40400541340-cit/DC, application/octet-stream
Unable to delete directory /xxx/1_25/staging/nlm:icid-40400541340-cit.

Underlying cause may be in https://jira.lyrasis.org/projects/FCREPO/issues/FCREPO-3191

Doron Shalvi / Calvin Xu: now that a fix for the related ticket has been committed to 'master' (https://jira.lyrasis.org/browse/FCREPO-3191), would you be able to test if the issue in this ticket has also been resolved?

yes, the issue seems to be fixed after we tested with the latest migration utility. We also added more inodes on our filesystem during the last round of testing. So far we have tested 8 million objects migration without issue in both akurba and legacy type.
